hypothesis: If no cataclysm ever desolated the whole world and the succession by generation was never broken, then at every stage boundary of the Phanerozoic a substantial share of the marine animal genera present must cross into the next stage, and survivors must be found in every major animal phylum even at the worst boundary.
pass_criterion: Using PBDB occs/diversity stage-level tables for marine Animalia genera (Phanerozoic) and the same table for each of nine marine animal phyla/classes (Mollusca, Brachiopoda, Arthropoda, Echinodermata, Cnidaria, Bryozoa, Porifera, Annelida, Chordata), define for each stage i the boundary-crossing fraction C_i = (X_bt + X_Ft) / (X_bt + X_Ft + X_bL + X_FL), the share of genera present in stage i that are also recorded after it (range-through or first-appearing and continuing). Exclude the two youngest stages (Recent edge). Pass if (1) the minimum C_i over all retained Phanerozoic stage boundaries is >= 0.10 (at no point did fewer than one in ten marine genera survive), AND (2) at the stage with the minimum C_i, at least 7 of the 9 phyla/classes have C_i > 0 (survivors in at least seven major lineages), AND (3) the median C_i over all stages is >= 0.5. Verdict 'supports' if all three hold; 'mixed' if (1) and (2) hold but (3) fails, or if (1) fails only marginally (0.05 <= min C_i < 0.10) while (2) holds; 'refutes' if any boundary has min C_i < 0.05 or fewer than 7 of 9 lineages have survivors at the worst boundary.
fail_criterion: Refuted if the fossil record contains a stage boundary across which fewer than 5% of marine animal genera persist, or at which survivors are absent from three or more of the nine major lineages, which would indicate a near-total biotic reset incompatible with unbroken descent. The Precambrian part of the claim ('long before the Silurian') cannot be tested with this data and is excluded from the verdict.
interpretation: Darwin's 'cataclysm desolating the whole world' is read as an event after which (nearly) no lineages persist, detectable as a stage boundary crossed by very few genera in very few lineages. 'The ordinary succession by generation has never once been broken' is tested only for the Phanerozoic marine record, where stage-level genus ranges exist; the Precambrian ancestry 'long before the Silurian' is outside what occurrence data can show. Boundary-crossing fractions are biased downward by incomplete sampling (Signor-Lipps and Lazarus effects), which makes the test conservative with respect to the claim. Thresholds of 10% and 7/9 lineages are deliberately lenient about mass extinctions, which Darwin did not deny in degree, and strict about total desolation, which he denied.
